info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package guide is the AI that builds an agentic company with you, one measured step at a time.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's launch journey: the active curriculum's version and title, every step with its state, whether it is available, what blocks it and whether the Business AI can run it, the done/total/percent progress with the next step to take, and the org's analytics funnel folded in.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's launch journey: the active curriculum's
version and title, every step with its state, whether it is available, what
blocks it and whether the Business AI can run it, the done/total/percent
progress with the next step to take, and the org's analytics funnel folded in.
Auto-detect runs first, so a step the org has already completed elsewhere reads
done without anyone marking it.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's Business AI action ledger, most recent first: every "do it for me" tool call, the arguments it ran with, its result and whether it succeeded.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's Business AI action ledger, most recent
first: every "do it for me" tool call, the arguments it ran with, its result and
whether it succeeded. It is the audit-visible record of what the agent did on
the org's behalf, and the backing state for the "acted" auto-detect signal.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's funnel from the analytics lens plus the GTM recommendations derived from it.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's funnel from the analytics lens plus the GTM
recommendations derived from it. It is the Business AI's data-grounded read —
what the funnel is doing, and the next-best action to move its weakest stage. An
unreachable or silent warehouse answers available=false, never a fabricated
number.

get.summary: Returns the FULL authored brand blueprint — every principle, section, step, strategy and template WITH its enabled flag made explicit, including the disabled items the org-facing reads never see — plus the active version number, the brand key it is stored under and the item counts.
get.description:
Returns the FULL authored brand blueprint — every principle,
section, step, strategy and template WITH its enabled flag made explicit,
including the disabled items the org-facing reads never see — plus the active
version number, the brand key it is stored under and the item counts. It is the
SuperAdmin authoring view of the platform blueprint, so it is refused 403 for
anyone else, including a per-org admin: the brand blueprint is shared platform
content, not a per-customer surface.

put.summary: Publish a new version of the brand blueprint
put.description:
Replaces the deployment's brand blueprint — the shared journey, sections, strategies and templates every org starts from — as a NEW VERSION, and answers the stored document with its key and version number. The previous versions are kept, so /blueprint/versions is a real recovery trail.

SuperAdmin ONLY. A per-org admin is 403: this is platform content, not a per-customer surface — the per-customer surface is /v1/guide/curriculum. The write is audited.

The body is a blueprint document accepted as YAML **or** JSON, which is the caller-visible reason it takes a raw body. It must parse AND validate — unique ids throughout, an acyclic step graph with no dangling dependencies, every step's section and every strategy's principle resolving to a real one — or it is 422 and never becomes active, leaving the version already serving authoritative. An empty body is 400 and one over 16 MiB is 413.

Edits are live: the next resolve reads the newest version. A stored document that is itself corrupt or schema-drifted does not block this write — the target is resolved without parsing what is there — so a bad version can always be published over.

get.summary: Returns the brand blueprint's version history — every stored version's number and edit time, newest first — which is the point-in-time-recovery and audit trail behind the authoring plane.
get.description:
Returns the brand blueprint's version history — every
stored version's number and edit time, newest first — which is the
point-in-time-recovery and audit trail behind the authoring plane. Metadata
only: the documents are not returned. SuperAdmin only, like the rest of this
plane. The history is listable even when the current stored document no longer
parses, so a schema-drifted row can still be diagnosed.

patch.summary: Edit — or retire — one item of the brand blueprint
patch.description:
Edits a single item of the brand blueprint by id and saves it as a NEW VERSION, answering the whole blueprint after the edit. `collection` is one of `sections`, `steps`, `strategies` or `templates`; anything else is 400, and an id that collection does not hold is 404. This is also the retire lever: `{"enabled": false}` takes an item out of every org's journey without deleting it or its history.

SuperAdmin ONLY, like the rest of the authoring plane; a per-org admin is 403. The write is audited.

The patch is a SHALLOW merge over the item's own top-level keys — a key you send replaces that key whole, a key you omit is left alone — and `id` is dropped from the patch before it is applied, so an edit can never rekey an item. That is why the body has no declarable shape: its keys are the patched item's, not this route's.

Fail-closed on the WHOLE document, not just the item: the blueprint is re-validated after the merge, so a patch that would dangle a dependency, break the step DAG or empty the journey is 422 and nothing is saved. An empty patch is 400 and one over 16 MiB is 413.

post.summary: Answers a founder's question about their launch journey as the Business AI coach: it grounds the reply in the org's REAL progress, its ranked available quests and its analytics funnel, and returns those candidate quests alongside so the caller can act on one.
post.description:
Answers a founder's question about their launch journey as the Business AI
coach: it grounds the reply in the org's REAL progress, its ranked available
quests and its analytics funnel, and returns those candidate quests alongside so
the caller can act on one. READ-ONLY — it advises and never runs a step, so it
cannot be talked into performing an action; the only executing path is POST
/v1/guide/steps/{id}/do. One AI completion per call, billed to the caller's own
payer.

example.message: what should I do next to get my first customers?

delete.summary: Clears the caller org's curriculum override and returns the journey it falls back to — the brand blueprint, else the embedded fixture.
delete.description:
Clears the caller org's curriculum override and returns the
journey it falls back to — the brand blueprint, else the embedded fixture.
Clearing an org that never set one is a no-op that answers the same default.

get.summary: Returns the journey the caller's org is actually running, and whether it comes from the org's OWN override (custom) or from the platform default — the brand blueprint, else the embedded fixture.
get.description:
Returns the journey the caller's org is actually running, and
whether it comes from the org's OWN override (custom) or from the platform
default — the brand blueprint, else the embedded fixture.

put.summary: Replace your org's journey with a curriculum you author
put.description:
Sets the caller org's OWN curriculum — the per-customer override — and answers the journey now in force with `custom: true`. The body is a curriculum document, and it is accepted as YAML **or** JSON: that is the caller-visible reason this takes a raw body rather than a declared shape. Whatever the syntax, the CANONICAL parsed form is what is stored, so the document the engine runs never depends on how it was written.

Fail-closed: a body that does not parse, or parses but is not a valid journey (unique step ids, no dangling or cyclic dependencies), is 422 and NEVER becomes active — the org keeps the journey it had. Requires a validated org: 401 without a principal, 403 without an org. An empty body is 400 and one over 256 KiB is 413.

This is tier one only. It overrides nothing but this org's own journey; the shared brand blueprint is a different surface with a different gate. DELETE the same path to drop the override and fall back to it.

get.summary: Returns the studio's portfolio operations rollup: stage, status, checklist progress, decisions waiting on people, latest evidence, failed runs, and spend for every venture operated by the studio organization.
get.description:
Returns the studio's portfolio operations rollup: stage, status,
checklist progress, decisions waiting on people, latest evidence, failed runs,
and spend for every venture operated by the studio organization.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's OBSERVED growth profile — the signal set, the classified growth stage, and the org's own key metrics.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's OBSERVED growth profile — the signal set, the
classified growth stage, and the org's own key metrics. It is a pure READ,
recomputed from the org's CURRENT state each request (real-time by pull): it
reuses the reconcile path (snapshotFor runs the detectors) for launch progress
and runs the growth probes (observe) for the signals — it never caches, never
runs a billable effect, never targets another org. Org-scoped on the validated
principal; fail-closed without one. It PRODUCES the profile and classifies the
stage; it decides NO recommendation (that is a later surface).

post.summary: Have the Business AI actually do the step for you
post.description:
Executes one step of the caller org's journey through that principal's OWN tool plane and answers the action log — `{step, events, state}` — so the caller sees every tool call the agent made and where the step ended up. This is the ONE executing path in guide: suggest and chat advise, this acts, and the work is charged to the calling principal's ledger.

Ask for it live and the same actions arrive as Server-Sent Events instead, on either of two triggers — `Accept: text/event-stream` or `?stream=1`. The stream opens with a comment, emits one frame per action as it happens, and closes with an `end` frame carrying `ok` and the final state. The streamed run is detached and bounded at 120 seconds, so it finishes on its own clock once the response has begun.

An agent that FAILS is not a failed request: the JSON answer still comes back 200 with `error` beside the events it did manage, and the stream still ends with `ok:false`. The refusals are the ones before the agent runs — 409 with `{error, step, blockedBy}` for a step whose dependencies are unfinished, 404 for an id the journey does not contain, 401 without a principal and 403 without an org.

post.summary: Marks one step of the caller org's journey complete and returns the refreshed journey.
post.description:
Marks one step of the caller org's journey complete and returns the
refreshed journey.

Dependency-GATED, exactly as start is: a step whose prerequisites are unfinished
is refused 409 carrying {error, step, blockedBy} naming what is in the way.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the step's id, as it appears in the journey (e.g. "gsuite").

post.summary: Returns one step of the caller org's journey to todo — clearing a manual mark or a skip — and returns the refreshed journey.
post.description:
Returns one step of the caller org's journey to todo — clearing a
manual mark or a skip — and returns the refreshed journey. Reset is never
dependency-gated. Auto-detect runs on the next read, so a step the org has in
fact completed elsewhere goes straight back to done.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the step's id, as it appears in the journey (e.g. "gsuite").

post.summary: Marks one step of the caller org's journey skipped and returns the refreshed journey.
post.description:
Marks one step of the caller org's journey skipped and returns the
refreshed journey. Skipping is never dependency-gated — the founder is
declaring the step does not apply to them — so a step whose dependencies are
unfinished can still be skipped, and a skipped step counts as terminal for
everything downstream of it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the step's id, as it appears in the journey (e.g. "gsuite").

post.summary: Marks one step of the caller org's journey in progress and returns the refreshed journey.
post.description:
Marks one step of the caller org's journey in progress and returns the
refreshed journey.

Dependency-GATED: a step whose prerequisites are unfinished is refused 409
carrying {error, step, blockedBy}, where blockedBy names the exact steps in the
way — enough to render the reason without asking again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the step's id, as it appears in the journey (e.g. "gsuite").

get.summary: Returns the ENABLED tactics corpus for the caller's org: the tactics library narrowed by the explicit category/workload filters AND by the org's OBSERVED growth stage and capability signals (a tactic's tags are preconditions, so it surfaces only once the org can act on it).
get.description:
Returns the ENABLED tactics corpus for the caller's org: the tactics
library narrowed by the explicit category/workload filters AND by the org's
OBSERVED growth stage and capability signals (a tactic's tags are
preconditions, so it surfaces only once the org can act on it). Passing stage
PREVIEWS the corpus at that stage instead of the observed one. The content is
shared platform data — no org's records — and the read is never a billable
effect.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category filters to tactics in exactly this category.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description:
Stage previews the corpus at a chosen growth stage
(research|formed|launched|activated|scaling), overriding the org's observed
one. An unknown value is ignored and the observed stage stands.

parameters.name: workload
parameters.description: Workload filters to tactics with exactly this workload.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's next-best quests: the available, non-terminal steps of its journey ranked by how much downstream work each unblocks, each with the grounded reason it is a good next move and whether the Business AI can run it, plus the org's funnel and the GTM recommendations derived from it.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's next-best quests: the available, non-terminal
steps of its journey ranked by how much downstream work each unblocks, each with
the grounded reason it is a good next move and whether the Business AI can run
it, plus the org's funnel and the GTM recommendations derived from it. A
best-effort AI narrative over exactly those quests and numbers is included when
an AI plane is wired. READ-ONLY: it advises and never runs a step — the only
executing path is POST /v1/guide/steps/{id}/do.

get.summary: Returns every venture in the caller studio organization's portfolio that the caller is authorized to access, with its live checklist progress and shared studio templates.
get.description:
Returns every venture in the caller studio organization's
portfolio that the caller is authorized to access, with its live checklist

post.summary: Creates or imports a venture under the caller studio's portfolio, captures its thesis, sponsor, owner, initial budget and seed evidence, and enrolls its isolated venture organization in a versioned Guide playbook (defaulting to venture).
post.description:
Creates or imports a venture under the caller studio's portfolio,
captures its thesis, sponsor, owner, initial budget and seed evidence, and
enrolls its isolated venture organization in a versioned Guide playbook
(defaulting to venture). Repeated or interrupted calls with the same slug

get.summary: Returns one venture from the caller studio's portfolio by slug, including its setup checkpoints, live checklist progress, and shared templates.
get.description:
Returns one venture from the caller studio's portfolio by slug,
including its setup checkpoints, live checklist progress, and shared templates.

parameters.name: slug

post.summary: Executes a portfolio lifecycle operation on a venture (pause, resume, advance, form, export, sync, offboard, assign_member, or revoke_member) and updates its operational telemetry (spend, pending decisions, failed runs, latest evidence, or company formation ID).
post.description:
Executes a portfolio lifecycle operation on a venture
(pause, resume, advance, form, export, sync, offboard, assign_member, or

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Slug is the venture handle from the URL path.

args.description:
Args is the JSON the tool was called with, recorded as TEXT exactly as sent —
including whatever the AI drafted into it — so a run can be read back and
reproduced. It is a string, not an object.

createdAt.description:
CreatedAt is when the run was recorded, as Unix seconds. The ledger is read
newest-first on this column.

err.description: Err is why the run failed, when it did. Empty on a successful run.

id.description:
ID identifies this one execution. The ledger is append-only, so an id is
never reused and never updated.

ok.description:
OK is whether the tool ran to completion. It is the ledger's own verdict, not
the tool's opinion of the outcome — a tool that succeeded at reporting bad
news is ok.

result.description:
Result is the tool's own answer, likewise recorded as JSON text. Present on a
failed run too, where the tool answered but the answer was a refusal.

stepId.description: StepID is the checklist step the Business AI was acting on.

tool.description: Tool is the MCP tool that was dispatched, by name.

caseStudy.description: CaseStudy is one worked instance — somebody who ran it, and what happened.

how.description: How is the run book: the steps to execute the tactic.

slug.description: Slug is the post's address — the last path segment it is published at.

why.description:
Why is the mechanism: the reason the tactic works, stated as a principle
rather than as instructions.

brand.description:
Brand is the white-label key this playbook serves. Empty is the shared
default every unbranded deployment falls back to.

enabled.description:
Enabled is the whole-playbook lever. Absent reads as ON; an explicit false
makes resolution skip this playbook entirely and fall through to the next
tier, rather than serving an empty journey.

principles.description:
Principles are the fixed 64-archetype spine a tactic files under. It is
authored data an operator organises the corpus by; nothing in the checklist
engine reads it.

sections.description: Sections are the journey's ordered phases.

steps.description:
Steps are every checklist item, disabled ones included — this is the authored
document, not the projection an org runs.

strategies.description: Strategies are the tactics corpus the recommendation reads narrow.

templates.description: Templates are the reusable prompts and snippets steps reference by id.

title.description: Title is the playbook's name as a person reads it.

version.description:
Version is the playbook's own name for this edition of its content, chosen by
whoever authored it. It travels onto every journey projected from it. The
store's numeric revision is a separate value and lives beside it.

steps.description:
Steps are the enabled steps in authoring order. Order is the tiebreak the
next-step logic walks, so it is part of the contract rather than cosmetic.

title.description: Title is the playbook's name as it heads the checklist.

version.description:
Version identifies the authored playbook this journey was projected from, so
two orgs on different playbooks can be told apart. It is the blueprint's own
`version` string, not the store's numeric revision.

available.description:
Available separates "this org has no traffic" from "we could not ask". False
means the warehouse was unreachable or the org has emitted nothing at all, and
every count below is then a placeholder zero rather than a measurement — a
caller must read this before reading any of them.

orders.description: Orders counts completed orders in the window — purchases, not carts started.

pageviews.description:
Pageviews counts page events in the window, one per view rather than per
person, so a single visitor reading ten pages counts ten.

revenue.description:
Revenue is the sum of the amounts those orders reported, in whatever currency
the beacon stamped on them (major units, e.g. 49.5 for $49.50) — NOT cents,
and not converted to a single currency. Contrast revenueCents on the profile,
which is the money of record.

signups.description:
Signups counts completed signups in the window, the step where an anonymous
visitor becomes somebody with an account.

visitors.description:
Visitors is the number of DISTINCT people seen in the window, counted by the
beacon's distinct id — so it is unique visitors, not sessions and not views.

windowDays.description:
WindowDays is the length of the trailing window every count covers, so a
reader knows whether 40 signups is a month or a day.

args.description:
Args are the tool's default arguments, merged under whatever the caller
passes at run time, so a step ships with the arguments that make it work.

deps.description:
Dependencies are step ids that must be done/skipped before this step is
available. The wire key is `deps` (the blueprint contract); the Go field keeps
its descriptive name.

detail.description: Detail is the juncture — what the Guide explains, or asks for, at this step.

draft.description:
Draft, when set, is the prompt the embedded AI answers first; its output is
folded into one of Args before the tool runs, so the model writes the
content and the tool only delivers it.

draftInto.description: DraftInto names the argument the drafted text lands in. Empty means "brief".

enabled.description:
Enabled is the admin on/off lever. A NIL pointer reads as ENABLED (absence ==
on): a legacy/org curriculum that omits the field keeps every step, and only an
explicit `enabled: false` (an admin disable) drops a step from the journey. See
on() in blueprint.go and the Blueprint.Curriculum() projection.

id.description:
ID is the stable slug the whole plane addresses this step by — the value in
`deps`, in `next`, in the progress rows, and in the URL of every step route.
Renaming it orphans an org's recorded progress for this step.

section.description:
Section is the id of the phase this step groups under. A disabled section
takes its steps out of the journey with it.

signal.description:
Signal, when set, names a machine detector (detect.go). When the detector
reports the org's real state present, the step auto-marks done.

title.description: Title is the one-line quest as a person reads it in the checklist.

tool.description:
Tool, when set, names the MCP tool the Business AI runs for "do it for me".
A step with no tool can only be completed by a person; it is the field the
`automatable` flag on every projection of this step is derived from.

enabled.description:
Enabled is the admin lever. Absent reads as ON; an explicit false withdraws
the template from org-facing reads.

id.description: ID is the slug a step references to pull this template in.

title.description: Title names the template in the authoring plane and in a picker.

domain.description: the growth / go-to-market domain it governs

slug.description: stable identifier a tactic files under

detail.description: Detail is what this phase of the journey is for, in prose.

enabled.description:
Enabled is the admin lever. Absent reads as ON, so only an explicit false
turns a phase off — and it takes every step filed under it out of the
journey, not just the heading.

id.description: ID is the slug a step's `section` names to file itself under this phase.

order.description:
Order places the phase in the journey, ascending. Ties fall back to
authoring order, and an omitted order sorts as 0 — ahead of everything.

title.description: Title is the phase heading a person reads above its steps.

action.description: Action is the tactic itself: the thing to go and do, stated imperatively.

blog.description: Blog is the tactic's long-form explainer; absent for tactics that have none.

category.description:
Category is the growth discipline the tactic belongs to — the axis
`?category=` narrows the corpus on, and one of the facets a caller browses by.

enabled.description:
Enabled is the admin lever. Absent reads as ON; an explicit false drops the
tactic from every org-facing corpus read while leaving it in the document.

era.description: Era separates an AI-era tactic (`modern`) from a classical one (`heritage`).

id.description: ID is the tactic's stable slug, unique across the corpus.

principle.description: Principle is the spine slug this tactic files under (a Principle.Slug).

source.description: Source is where the tactic came from — the attribution a reader is owed.

tags.description:
Tags are PRECONDITIONS, not labels — every one must be satisfied by the org's
observed profile before the tactic surfaces, so an untagged tactic is
universally applicable. Two vocabularies: `stage:<research|formed|launched|
activated|scaling>` reads the org's growth stage, `has:<capability>` reads an
observed signal.

workload.description:
Workload is how much effort running the tactic costs, so a corpus can be
narrowed to what an org has the hands for right now.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the venture was first registered in the portfolio, as Unix seconds.

evidence.description: Evidence lists the source citations and evidence URIs attached to the venture.

failedRuns.description: FailedRuns is how many specialist or automation runs have failed and await retry or review.

formationId.description: FormationID is the legal entity formation identifier from /v1/company once the venture advances to formation.

imported.description: Imported is true when the venture was imported into the studio rather than started from scratch.

initialBudgetMicroUSD.description: InitialBudgetMicroUSD is the initial venture budget in integer micro-USD, allocated at creation.

latestEvidence.description: LatestEvidence is the most recently recorded evidence citation or URI for this venture.

members.description: Members lists the teammate subjects explicitly assigned access to this venture.

owner.description: Owner is the venture lead (person or lead agent handle) accountable for executing the playbook.

pendingDecisions.description: PendingDecisions is how many research decisions, role proposals, or external actions await human approval.

playbookVersion.description: PlaybookVersion is the version string of the Guide curriculum enrolled for this venture.

progress.description: Progress is the venture's live checklist completion read from its isolated organization store.

resumed.description: Resumed is true when a repeated or interrupted create call resumed an existing venture without duplicating budget or team.

setup.description: Setup holds the idempotent setup operation checkpoints for this venture.

slug.description: Slug is the venture's unique handle inside the studio portfolio.

spendMicroUSD.description: SpendMicroUSD is the cumulative spend recorded against this venture in integer micro-USD.

sponsor.description: Sponsor is the studio partner or executive sponsoring the venture.

stage.description: Stage is the venture's position in the studio funnel: intake, discovery, validation, formation, or scaling.

status.description: Status is the venture's operating state: active, paused, forming, formed, or offboarded.

studioOrg.description: StudioOrg is the parent studio organization operating the portfolio.

templates.description: Templates are the shared studio templates from the playbook visible in this venture.

thesis.description: Thesis is the falsifiable venture hypothesis being tested before entity formation.

title.description: Title is the human-readable name of the venture.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is when the venture record was last updated, as Unix seconds.

ventureOrg.description: VentureOrg is the isolated organization namespace holding this venture's private progress, documents, runs, and secrets.

budgetAllocated.description: BudgetAllocated is true once the initial micro-USD budget has been committed, preventing duplicate allocation.

members.description: Members lists the teammate subjects explicitly assigned access to this venture.

orgProvisioned.description: OrgProvisioned is true once the venture's isolated organization store has been opened.

playbookEnrolled.description: PlaybookEnrolled is true once the versioned curriculum has been persisted in the venture's store.

revokedMembers.description: RevokedMembers lists teammate subjects whose seat access to this venture has been revoked.

teamSeeded.description: TeamSeeded is true once the venture's team roster has been enrolled.

brand.description:
Brand is the white-label key this revision was authored under; empty is the
shared base playbook. Revisions of two brands never share a number line.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is when this revision was written, as Unix seconds — the "who
changed the playbook, and when" half of the audit trail.

version.description:
Version is the store's own revision counter for that brand, starting at 1 for
the seeded playbook and incrementing on every edit. Nothing is overwritten, so
the highest number is the live one and every lower number is still readable.
It is not the playbook's authored `version` string.

data.description: Data is the most-recent actions first, capped at listActionsLimit.

funnel.description:
Funnel is the org's trailing-30-day traffic → signups → orders from the
shared analytics warehouse; available is false when it has emitted nothing.

recommendations.description: Recommendations are the next-best GTM actions derived from that funnel.

principles.description:
Principles is how many spine archetypes the playbook carries (64 in the
shipped corpus).

sections.description: Sections is how many phases the journey has.

steps.description:
Steps is how many checklist items the playbook holds, DISABLED ONES INCLUDED
— this counts the authored document, not the journey an org runs, so it is
normally larger than the `total` on a progress view.

strategies.description: Strategies is how many tactics the corpus holds, again counting disabled ones.

templates.description: Templates is how many reusable prompts the playbook carries.

brand.description:
Brand is the blueprint key the history belongs to — this deployment's brand,
or "" (the base blueprint) when the brand has no row of its own.

versions.description:
Versions are the stored versions, newest first: metadata only, never the
documents.

blueprint.description:
Blueprint is the whole authored document, including items disabled for the
org-facing reads, with every enabled flag written out explicitly.

brand.description:
Brand is the key this blueprint is stored under — the deployment's brand, or
"" for the shared base blueprint it falls back to.

counts.description: Counts summarises how many items each collection holds.

version.description:
Version is the active stored version number (1 is the seed). Each edit
appends a new one; nothing is ever overwritten.

message.description:
Message is the founder's question for the Business AI. Required; trimmed,
and clipped to 4 KiB so a caller cannot amplify the AI prompt.

funnel.description: Funnel is the org's trailing-window traffic → signups → orders.

reply.description:
Reply is the coach's answer, grounded only in the quests and funnel below.
When no AI plane is reachable it is the deterministic reply naming the top
real quest — never silence, never invention.

suggestions.description: Suggestions are the current candidate quests, ranked best-first.

count.description: Count is how many tactics survived every filter.

stage.description:
Stage is the growth stage the tag join ran at — the org's observed stage, or
the one ?stage= previewed.

strategies.description: Strategies are the surviving tactics, in corpus authoring order.

evidence.description: Evidence lists initial source citations or evidence URIs for the venture.

imported.description: Imported marks whether this venture is being imported from an existing workspace.

initialBudgetMicroUSD.description: InitialBudgetMicroUSD is the initial budget allocated to the venture in integer micro-USD.

members.description: Members optionally assigns initial teammate subjects access to this venture.

owner.description: Owner names the venture lead (person or lead agent handle) driving the venture.

playbook.description: Playbook selects a brand playbook name (such as "venture") or supplies a raw YAML/JSON curriculum document; empty defaults to "venture".

slug.description: Slug is the venture's unique handle inside the studio portfolio (e.g. "vet-clinic-scheduling").

sponsor.description: Sponsor names the studio partner or executive sponsoring the venture.

stage.description: Stage sets the initial studio funnel stage (intake, discovery, validation, formation, scaling); defaults to "intake".

teamSeeded.description: TeamSeeded marks whether the venture's initial agent roster has been seeded.

thesis.description: Thesis is the falsifiable venture hypothesis to test before entity formation.

title.description: Title is the human-readable name of the venture.

ventureOrg.description: VentureOrg optionally names the explicit venture organization slug; when omitted it defaults to "<studioOrg>--<slug>".

curriculum.description: Curriculum is the enabled journey: its version, title and ordered steps.

custom.description:
Custom is true when the org's OWN curriculum override is active; false when
the journey comes from the brand blueprint or the embedded fixture.

Custom is true when the org replaced the shared playbook with one of its own
— the difference between "everyone's checklist" and "the one you authored".

funnel.description:
Funnel is the org's analytics lens, present only where the read asked for it
— absent means it was not requested, never that the org has no traffic.

progress.description: Progress is how far through the journey the org is.

steps.description:
Steps are every enabled step with the org's own state folded in, in
authoring order.

title.description: Title is the playbook's name as it heads the checklist.

version.description:
Version identifies the playbook this journey came from, so a caller can tell
that the checklist itself changed under them.

activeVentures.description: ActiveVentures is how many ventures are currently in active execution.

failedRuns.description: FailedRuns is the total count of failed runs across all ventures in the portfolio.

formedVentures.description: FormedVentures is how many ventures have advanced to legal entity formation.

offboardedVentures.description: OffboardedVentures is how many ventures have been offboarded from the studio.

pausedVentures.description: PausedVentures is how many ventures are currently paused.

pendingDecisions.description: PendingDecisions is the total count of decisions, role proposals, and external actions waiting on people across the portfolio.

studioOrg.description: StudioOrg is the studio organization whose portfolio is summarized.

totalBudgetMicroUSD.description: TotalBudgetMicroUSD is the sum of initial budgets allocated across all ventures in integer micro-USD.

totalSpendMicroUSD.description: TotalSpendMicroUSD is the cumulative spend across all ventures in integer micro-USD.

totalVentures.description: TotalVentures is the total number of ventures registered in the studio portfolio.

ventures.description: Ventures is the per-venture operational rollup ordered by creation time.

funnel.description:
Funnel is what the org's analytics observed over the trailing window. Read
its `available` first: an org with no analytics reports zeros here, and zero
traffic and no measurement are different facts.

launchProgress.description:
LaunchProgress is the org's own position in the launch checklist, folded in
so a profile carries both what the org has BUILT and what it has DONE.

records.description:
Records is how many business records the org holds — the volume that tells a
real book of customers from an empty account. It feeds the `customers`
signal, which crosses at a threshold rather than at one row.

revenueCents.description:
RevenueCents is the org's money OF RECORD — what its books say, in whole
cents, never a float and never a display string. This is the number the
scaling stage is decided on; funnel.revenue is the beacon's separate,
unreconciled view of the same business. Zero when the org has none, and also
zero when the books could not be read, which is why the `revenue` signal
beside it is the thing to trust.

keyMetrics.description:
KeyMetrics are the org's OWN numbers behind those signals — never another
org's, and never a platform aggregate.

signals.description:
Signals is what was observed of the org right now, one boolean per probe.
A probe that could not be run reports FALSE, not absent — the shape is stable
so a caller never has to tell a missing key from a negative answer, and the
cost is that "not observed" and "not there" look alike here. Keys are the
probe names, including the `module:<name>` and `connected:<provider>`
families.

stage.description:
Stage is how far the business itself has got — formed, launched, activated or
scaling — decided purely from the signals below, and by what the org has
ACHIEVED rather than what it has configured. It reads the STRONGEST evidence
present, so money of record makes an org scaling even if an earlier rung's
signal was never observed. It is unrelated to checklist progress.

done.description:
Done counts steps that are FINISHED — done and skipped alike, since a step
the org deliberately passed over is not still owed. It therefore rises when
somebody skips, which is the intended reading of a checklist.

next.description:
Next is the id of the step to do next: the first available, unfinished step
in authoring order. Empty when the journey is complete, and also empty when
every remaining step is blocked by a dependency.

percent.description:
Percent is done/total as a whole number 0-100, rounded, so a caller renders
a bar without recomputing it. Total zero reads as 0.

total.description:
Total is how many steps this org's journey holds — the ENABLED steps of the
playbook, so it shrinks when an operator disables one and does not match the
authored step count.

args.description:
Args are the tool's default arguments, merged under whatever the caller
passes at run time.

automatable.description: Automatable is true when the Business AI can run this step (it names a tool).

available.description: Available is true when every dependency is done or skipped.

blockedBy.description: BlockedBy lists the unfinished dependencies keeping the step unavailable.

deps.description:
Dependencies are step ids that must be done/skipped before this step is
available. The wire key is `deps` (the blueprint contract).

detail.description: Detail is the prose/juncture — what the Guide asks or explains here.

draft.description:
Draft, when set, is the prompt the embedded AI answers first; its output is
folded into one of Args before the tool runs.

draftInto.description: DraftInto names the argument the drafted text lands in. Empty means "brief".

enabled.description: Enabled is the admin on/off lever; absent reads as enabled.

id.description: ID is the step's id, as it appears in the journey (e.g. "gsuite").

section.description: Section is the phase (section id) this step groups under.

signal.description: Signal names the machine detector that auto-marks this step done.

source.description: Source records what marked the state: manual, auto (detected) or agent.

state.description: State is the step's per-org lifecycle state: todo|in_progress|done|skipped.

title.description: Title is the one-line quest as a person reads it in the checklist.

tool.description:
Tool is the MCP tool the Business AI runs for "do it for me". A step naming
none can only be completed by a person.

action.description: Action is the tactic itself: the thing to go and do.

category.description:
Category is the growth discipline the tactic belongs to — the axis
`?category=` narrows on.

id.description: ID is the tactic's stable slug in the corpus.

tags.description:
Tags are the PRECONDITIONS this tactic already satisfied to appear in the
answer — `stage:<name>` and `has:<capability>` predicates over the org's
observed profile. They are carried back so a caller can show why a tactic
surfaced, not so it can filter again.

workload.description:
Workload is how much effort running the tactic costs, so a corpus can be cut
to what the org has the hands for.

funnel.description: Funnel is the org's trailing-window traffic → signups → orders.

narrative.description:
Narrative is the AI's grounded prose over those quests and numbers. Absent
when no AI plane is wired or the completion failed — never fabricated.

next.description:
Next is the id of the single next step the static journey names — the
linear answer the ranked Suggestions refine.

recommendations.description: Recommendations are the next-best GTM actions derived from that funnel.

suggestions.description:
Suggestions are the available, non-terminal quests ranked best-first by how
much downstream work each unblocks.

automatable.description:
Automatable is true when the step names a tool, so the Business AI can do it
rather than only describe it.

detail.description: Detail is the step's own prose — what it asks for.

rationale.description:
Rationale is why this step is being suggested NOW, written for the person
reading it. It explains the ranking, not the step.

stepId.description:
StepID is the checklist step being recommended — the id every step route
takes, so a caller can act on the suggestion directly.

title.description: Title is the step's own one-line quest.

unlocks.description:
Unlocks is how many downstream steps completing this one immediately makes
available (its leverage) — the primary ranking key.

actions.description: Actions are the Business AI action ledger rows recorded inside the venture's isolated store.

playbookVersion.description: PlaybookVersion is the enrolled curriculum version at export time.

steps.description: Steps are the venture's checklist steps with their recorded states at export time.

ventureOrg.description: VentureOrg is the isolated venture organization identifier.

action.description: Action is the lifecycle operation to perform: pause, resume, advance, form, export, sync, offboard, assign_member, or revoke_member.

failedRuns.description: FailedRuns optionally updates the count of failed runs requiring attention.

formationId.description: FormationID optionally records the /v1/company formation identifier when action is "form".

latestEvidence.description: LatestEvidence optionally records a new evidence citation or URI on the venture.

member.description: Member names the teammate subject to assign or revoke when action is "assign_member" or "revoke_member".

pendingDecisions.description: PendingDecisions optionally updates the count of decisions waiting on human review.

slug.description: Slug is the venture handle from the URL path.

spendMicroUSD.description: SpendMicroUSD optionally adds or updates recorded venture spend in integer micro-USD.

stage.description: Stage optionally updates the venture's funnel stage (intake, discovery, validation, formation, scaling).

teamSeeded.description: TeamSeeded optionally marks the venture's agent roster checkpoint complete.

export.description: Export is populated when action is "export", carrying the portable snapshot of the venture's checklist and action ledger.

venture.description: Venture is the updated venture record after the lifecycle operation.

ventures.description: Ventures are the studio organization's ventures in creation order, each with live progress.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
